pages.title: Hulls and Pressure
pages.text: Deep water crushes blocks. Every block has a maximum depth, and a ship is only as strong as its weakest block. The **Pressure Barometer** compares the pressure on the ship to what the weakest block can take. Goggles show a block's hull tier: fragile, standard or reinforced.

Past its limit a block gives way. Above a certain depth the room just floods through the hole. Far deeper, a failing block implodes the whole ship. The **Industrial Alarm** flashes and sounds faster every 5 m you sink past the safe depth. Tune it all in the Deep Seas config.

pages.title: Pressure Barometer
pages.text: Shows depth and pressure. Attach a Display Link to broadcast depth and hull state to a Display Board.

pages.title: Iron Pressurized Glass
pages.text: Windows need special glass. Glass, Iron and Copper Pressurized Glass resist pressure; plain glass does not.

Hull limits can be tuned. Deep Seas has a max depth multiplier that scales every block, and per-block depths are stored in **config/submarine\_hull.json**. Windows are the usual weak point, so use pressurized glass. Goggles on a block show its tier.

A dry interior needs a sealed hull. An **Electrolyzer** turns water into oxygen, an **Oxygen Diffuser** spreads it through the ship (give it a redstone signal). The Electrolyzer runs on FE power, see [#](2E5AAC)[Electricity](entry://industry/electricity)[#](), or you can put a Shaft in its module slot and spin it directly.

pages.title: Electrolyzer
pages.text: Water in, oxygen out. Accepts FE, or a shaft in the module slot for plain Create rotation.

To leave the ship underwater, build an airlock from two **Decompression Chambers** joined by pipes and a pump. Flood the airlock before opening the outer door deep down, or the sea crushes it in. Reverse the pump to dry it again.

pages.title: Decompression Chamber
pages.text: An airlock valve. Pipe water in at the back to flood a room, or out to empty it.

**Create: Deep Seas, Lava Fix** patches a bug: players inside a sealed submarine submerged in lava no longer take fire or lava damage, since the interior is dry. Nothing to set up.\
